Order 
This bail application is filed under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the first accused in Crime No.220 of 2025 of Edakkad Police Station, Kannur,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 r/w. Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3. According to the prosecution, during the period from 27.01.2021 to 07.10.2021, the accused had in furtherance of their common intention to cheat, received a total amount of Rs.47,85,000/- from the defacto complainant by way of eight installments by offering the job of Assistant Professor in Commerce at SN College, Kannur for a total amount of Rs.55,00,000/- and thereafter the accused neither arranged the job nor returned the amount and thereby committed the offences alleged.
Petitioner was arrested on 27.06.2025 and he has been in custody since then.
4.

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the BAIL APPL. NO. 9260 OF 2025 2025:KER:59091 learned Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
6. Petitioner is alleged to have conspired with the 2 nd accused to collect money for providing employment to the defacto complainant as an Assistant Professor at SN College, Kannur.

Though the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the quantum of amount allegedly received by the petitioner is minor when compared to the quantum received by the 2nd accused, who is in fact connected with the management of SN College, Kannur, I am of the view that the quantum received by each person is not by itself a determinative factor regarding the crime.

The role of each accused is Vaishak.V vs State Of Kerala on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79431959/
2 significant and therefore the said contention is not legally tenable.

sentences.text: However, since the 2 nd accused had approached this Court in Crl.M.C.No.6136 of 2025 and based on mediation talks existing between the parties, coercive proceedings against him has been kept in abeyance, I am of the view that petitioner's custody need not be continued especially since he was arrested on 27.06.2025.
In such circumstances, I am of the view that petitioner can be released on bail on conditions.

In the result, this application is allowed on the following conditions:-
BAIL APPL. NO. 9260 OF 2025 2025:KER:59091 (a) Petitioner shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the court having jurisdiction.
(b) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.
(c) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses.
(d) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
(e) Petitioner shall not leave India without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.

Sd/-
BECHU KURIAN THOMAS, JUDGE RKM BAIL APPL.
